content: Clemastine is an antihistamine prescribed to alleviate symptoms of hay fever and allergies. These symptoms include itchy skin, hives, sneezing, a runny nose, and red, itchy, or tearing eyes. It may also be prescribed for other uses, so consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Clemastine is available in regular and extended-release tablets, as well as in liquid form, and is taken orally. Typically, it is taken twice daily. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take clemastine exactly as directed. Do not take more or less than prescribed, and do not take it more frequently than instructed. Extended-release tablets should not be crushed or chewed; swallow them whole. Consult your doctor before giving this medication to children under 12 years of age. Before taking clemastine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to clemastine or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially those for colds, hay fever, allergies, depression, seizures, muscle relaxation, pain relief (narcotics), sedation, sleep aids, tranquilizers, or vitamins. Do not take clemastine if you have used an MAO inhibitor in the past two weeks. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had asthma, lung disease, diabetes, glaucoma, ulcers, difficulty urinating (due to an enlarged prostate), heart disease, high blood pressure, seizures, or an overactive thyroid gland. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking clemastine, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking clemastine. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can increase the drowsiness caused by this medication, so avoid consuming alcohol while taking clemastine. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Clemastine may cause side effects. Minor side effects include drowsiness, dry mouth, nose, and throat, dizziness, upset stomach, chest congestion, and headache. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Severe side effects include dry mouth, excitement (especially in children), nervousness, enlarged pupils, and increased sensitivity to sunlight. If you experience any of these severe symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store clemastine in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
